bifrost: springboard/ui/src/fileaction.rs (ActionRegistry, ActionId, FileAction); springboard/ui/src/actionrequest.rs (ActionRequest, Outcome); springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs (context_menu, ContextAction); springboard/src/files/mod.rs (Files app context menu); springboard/src/files/fs.rs (Files operations); springboard/src/bare/docbroker.rs (document grants)
summary: Apple's framework is one extension point: a File Provider extension adds actions to the long-press context menu of its own files in the system document browser, and shows a custom view controller to finish each action. BifrOSt now has pure models for the action side (springboard/ui/src/fileaction.rs: typed action identifiers, a registry per app, and the rule that picks the actions for a selection by uniform type; springboard/ui/src/actionrequest.rs: the request that a hosted view completes or cancels). It still has no extension process, no action surface in the Files browser, and no provider domain, so an app cannot yet add actions to Files.

gaps: No extension point through which a third-party app adds actions to the Files browser's item context menu (the core of this framework); the registry model exists but nothing consults it.
No hosted extension process that shows a custom action UI over the Files browser and completes or cancels a selected action; ActionRequest models the lifecycle only.
No provider domain model: the system browser cannot list an app's own files as a browsable location.
No system-wide registry of action identifiers that the shell consults and delivers to apps; identifiers are typed but not routed.
No authentication-error hand-off for file actions against remote or cloud providers.
